I am 50 this year, and I have been farming my family's 8 mu of land in Quzhou County since I was young. I only finished primary school, so I don't read those technical manuals or calculate fancy formulas — I watch what my neighbors do and remember what happened on my own fields in previous years. Last October I planted wheat on all 8 mu using Jimai 22, the same improved variety that Lao Zhang across the road uses, because it has done well here and I know it. Right now the wheat is greening up after winter, so the season has started. I irrigated once before the cold set in, and I will water two more times this spring — at jointing and when the grain is filling. At planting I spread about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, and I will topdress with urea when the wheat starts growing fast, same as every year. I already sprayed herbicide in autumn, and I will spray once or twice more if I see aphids or rust.

I thought about planting some cotton because my cousin mentioned prices were not bad, but my wife and I do not have enough labor for picking cotton in autumn, and the wheat-maize double crop is our safety net — we always have flour and corn meal at home, and we can sell the surplus. So all 8 mu will stay in wheat and then maize. After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant Denghai 605 hybrid maize the same day or the next. Everyone buys fresh hybrid seed every year — you cannot save it. I will not till the soil for maize anymore; I plant directly into the wheat stubble with the no-till machine to save time in that tight window. For corn I use a bit less fertilizer than wheat — about one bag of compound per mu and some urea when the plants are knee-high — and I will irrigate twice if the summer rains do not come. I expect around 420 kg of wheat per mu and about 480 kg of corn per mu in a normal year. I have to be careful with input costs because my daughter is still in school, but I also know that cutting back too much on fertilizer is risky — I would rather waste a little money than lose the whole crop.
